meta.setIdentity: CHILI LAB urban romance for Japanese listeners in their 20s and 30s: fresh, lovable and lightly sweet without becoming bright J-pop or a sugary R&B ballad. The emotional center is the shy pleasure of seeing each other through a camera for the first time.
meta.romanceTonePolicy: Keep the relationship young and slightly awkward: teasing, missed timing, small compliments, playful framing, accidental laughter and one photo becoming privately precious. Sweetness is carried by groove, vocal color and objects rather than direct declarations.
meta.genrePolicy: Chill rap / jazz-hop, neo-soul chill rap, tape-soul alt-R&B, soft 2-step garage, acoustic soul-hop, broken beat, minimal microhouse soul and dream-soul are internal variations under one CHILI LAB identity.
meta.instrumentPolicy: Rotate muted guitar, vibraphone, marimba, Wurlitzer, upright piano, tape piano, mellow flute, cello pizzicato, clean electric guitar, soft analog cloud and dub bass. Avoid Rhodes as an automatic default.
meta.vocalPolicy: Mature but youthful-feeling close vocals: warm tenor-baritone, light smoky male chest-mix, soft alto, clear warm mezzo and playful rhythmic mezzo. Use gentle smiles in delivery, small melodic lifts and restrained breathiness; no belt or falsetto climax.
meta.killingPointPolicy: Every track has one subtle 8-15 second signature moment, prioritizing hook variation, vocal handoff or a short 2-4 note instrumental answer.
meta.energyArc: curious reunion -> playful portraits -> comfortable teasing -> a quietly precious shared image -> open-ended goodbye

songs.title: You Brought It
songs.centralImage: a small silver camera hanging from a wrist at the station exit
songs.seasonMoment: late October, early afternoon outside a neighborhood station
songs.listenerSituation: he notices that she actually brought the little camera they joked about at the end of their last walk
songs.stylePrompt: CHILI LAB jazz-hop urban soul, 82 BPM, loose dry drums, muted guitar, upright bass and vibraphone. Warm tenor-baritone, close spoken-sung verses, soft chest tone and lightly smiling melodic hook. Keep the groove low-mid and playful, with a 3-note vibraphone answer after the title. Complete two-verse form with short bridge and final hook; short outro.
songs.excludePrompt: bright J-pop chorus, sugary R&B ballad, belt, falsetto climax, trap rolls, festival synths, giant vocal stack, long outro, heavy reverb
songs.lyrics:
[Intro]
Silver strap against your sleeve
You brought it

[Verse 1]
You come out past the ticket gate
Two minutes later than you said
Coffee in one hand, camera in the other
Like yesterday left something unfinished
I point at it before I say hello
You look down like you forgot it was there
Then lift it once by the little silver strap
And say, you asked for proof

[Hook]
You Brought It
That tiny camera with the scratched-up side
You Brought It
Now I have to stand where you tell me
I thought we were joking yesterday
You say maybe you were not
You Brought It

[Verse 2]
We pass the vending machines outside
You clean the lens on the edge of your sweater
I ask if you know what you are doing
You say enough to make me nervous
The shopping street is still half awake
A bakery pulls up its red awning
You turn the camera toward me once
Then lower it when I notice

[Hook Reprise]
You brought it after all
Now neither of us can pretend

[Bridge]
The strap swings between your fingers
Three silver flashes in the sun
You say walk first, pose later
That sounds easier for both of us

[Final Hook]
You Brought It
And somehow the whole street feels different
You Brought It
Like anything could become worth keeping
Not everything, not yet
Just maybe one good frame
You Brought It

[Outro]
The silver strap taps your sleeve
songs.vocalDesign: Warm tenor-baritone; conversational sing-rap in verses, slightly brighter melodic hook without pop belting.
songs.emotionDesign: Freshness comes from surprise and teasing rather than romantic declaration.
songs.durationDesign: Two full verses, compact reprise, short bridge and three audible title appearances; no extended outro.
songs.diversityDesign: Dry jazz-hop opener with vibraphone; no Rhodes and no female lead.
songs.killingPointDesign: After the second You Brought It, a 3-note vibraphone answer repeats once under the next line.
